A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same work. Their main text, equations, Figures 1–12, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original policy-evaluation experiments using simulated referrals and observed ICPSR recruitment networks, with results in Figures 3–12.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and their results in the main text and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The greedy allocation rule, population-level surrogate, probability-generating-function dynamic program, and round-budget selection procedure are unchanged. The revision concerns their theoretical justification and guarantee scope.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate simulated and realized referrals on the same ICPSR HIV, Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, Hepatitis, and Syphilis networks. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 8 and Figures 3–12 retain Const(k) for k in {2,3,5,10}, plus Greedy(alpha) and GreedyRemainder(alpha) for alpha in {0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0}. The revised explanation of greedy optimality does not change the evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Both versions use budget 200, discount factors {0.5,0.7,0.9}, initial frontier sizes {5,10,15}, and accumulated discounted reward. Referral construction and evaluation procedures in Section 8 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E4.justification: The simulated-versus-realized referral comparison assessing model misspecification and the discount-factor/frontier-size sweeps are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figures 3–12 report the same practice in both versions: 30 independent runs per configuration, means, and standard error bands. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting change is documented.

E6.justification: Figures 3–12 contain identical plotted results and uncertainty bands. Section 8.1 and the discussion retain the same findings, including shortcomings on Chlamydia and Gonorrhea at discount factor 0.9.

T1.justification: Section 5 withdraws the claimed exact reduction from Equation (2) to Equation (3), recasting it as a restriction to greedy within-round policies. Section 7 changes the stated comparison policy from the unrestricted optimum to the best greedy within-round policy. This substantially narrows the theoretical scope, although bound formulas and Appendix B–C proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion replaces the claim that multi-round planning reduces to choosing round budgets through greedy optimality with planning under a fixed greedy within-round rule. This materially narrows the claimed structural contribution; the abstract and introduction otherwise retain their original contributions.

C2.justification: A new Section 5 footnote explains that greedy maximizes immediate expected recruitment, whereas continuation value depends on the full next-frontier-size distribution. This adds an explicit theoretical limitation. Existing experimental interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the same distribution-construction procedure, mixture approximation and truncation details, Python/Slurm implementation information, and code/data access disclosures. Only the access footnotes' numbering changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning relative to stochastic control, online allocation, and approximate dynamic programming. References are repaginated without substantive changes.

P1.justification: Sections 5–9 receive targeted edits qualifying greedy optimality, including a rewritten explanatory paragraph and new footnote. V2 also adds an equal-contribution disclosure and updates version dates. The section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added explanation and footnote cause local text and equation reflow: Section 6 starts on page 5, and references start on page 10. Text beneath Figures 3–4 shifts, while all figures, captions, axes, legends, and the algorithm display remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves accuracy by acknowledging the greedy-policy restriction and narrowing the optimality claims in Sections 5, 7, and 9. The repair remains incomplete: Equations (2)–(3) reuse the same optimal-value notation, and the unchanged proof of Lemma C.7 still invokes single-round optimality to compare continuation values. The clearer claim scope is a real but limited quality gain.
